title: CRLR/78/2004 of IQBAL and ANR. Vs STATE

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
CRIMINAL REVISION No. 78/2004
Iqbal @ Karigar & Another ÖÖÖ Revisionists
Versus
State of Uttarakhand ÖÖÖ. Respondent
Mr. Dinesh Chauhan, Advocate, for the revisionists.
Smt. Mamta Bisht, AGA, for the State.
3rd September, 2012

Honíble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
 Facts, in brief, are that a Criminal Case No.
334/2003, State v. Yusuf & 2 Others, was proceeded in the
Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bageshwar, wherein three
accused persons, namely, Yusuf, Iqbal @ Karigar and Rais
Ahmad @ Champian were tried for the offences under Section
379 & 411 IPC. Learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bageshwer
vide his judgment and order dated 22.3.2004 convicted all the
three accused persons for the offence under Section 411 IPC
and sentenced each one of them to undergo imprisonment for a
period of one year and a fine of ` 500/- each. However, benefit
of doubt was extended to all the three accused persons and
they were acquitted from the charge of offence punishable
under Section 379 IPC. Feeling aggrieved, accused persons filed
two separate appeals before the Sessions Judge, Bageshwer.
Criminal Appeal No. 1/2004 was filed by Iqbal @ Karigar and
Rais Ahmad @ Champian i.e. present revisionists, while
Criminal Appeal No. 2/2004 was filed by Yusuf. Learned
Sessions Judge, Bageshwar affirmed the finding of conviction
and sentence awarded by the trial court and dismissed both the
aforesaid criminal appeals on 12.5.2004.
2. Feeling disgruntled, accused convicts filed two
separate criminal revisions before this Court. Criminal Revision
No. 79/2004, preferred by accused revisionist Yusuf was
dismissed on merit by this Court on 23.12.2011, and the

2
concurrent finding recorded by the courts below was affirmed.
Now, the instant revision has come up for hearing.
3. Heard learned Counsel for the parties and perused
the papers available on record.
4. Learned Counsel for the revisionists does not want to
press this revision on merit. He pleaded mercy of this Court on
the quantum of sentence only. He submitted that amount of
fine may appropriately be enhanced.
5. Considering the submissions of learned Counsel for
the revisionists that accused revisionists are living in abject
poverty and sending them to the gaol at this stage would push
their families in starvation, incident being very trivial in nature
and has happened more than ten years ago, this Court is
inclined to reduce the sentence of imprisonment awarded to the
accused revisionists. However, at the same time, the Court
cannot be oblivious of the fact that for the same offence and
sentence, Criminal Revision No. 79/2004, filed by another
accused Yusuf, has been dismissed by this Court on merits.
Learned Counsel for the revisionists, who was the Counsel on
behalf of Yusuf too, submitted that since Yusuf had completed
the sentence awarded by the trial court, therefore, he did not
extended any such argument regarding abject poverty, etc. as a
mitigating factor before this Court at the time of final argument.
Be that as it may, I find no mention of the fact that Yusuf by
that time had completed the sentence.
6. In the facts and circumstances of the case, this
Court deems it proper that sentence of six monthsí
imprisonment and a fine of rupees four thousand to each of the
accused revisionists shall serve the ends of justice. Impugned

3
judgments and orders are liable to be modified to this extent
only.
7. Resultantly, this revision is dismissed on merit.
However, on the quantum of sentence, it is partly allowed. The
impugned judgments and orders of the trial court and the
appellate court are affirmed with the modification of sentence
as indicated above. Accused revisionists shall be taken into
custody to serve out the modified sentence. The period during
which the revisionists were behind the bars at the time of
investigation, trial, appeal and during pendency of this revision
shall be adjusted. However, it is made clear that if the
revisionists fail to deposit the enhanced amount of fine, they
shall serve out the sentence as awarded by the trial court.
8. A copy of this judgment and order be sent to the trial
court for its compliance. Let the lower court record be also sent
back.
